findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote (“Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!”), at both widths
findings.fault: The pull quote is static, but it is set in logo blue. The tile's own palette reserves that colour for links and the button. In the specimen, blue means 'you can click this' on the PDF link below it and on the 'Get in touch' button, and it means 'emphasis' on the quote. So one look stands for two functions on the article page, and the next round would carry that over.
findings.who_objects: A reader on an article page. A large blue line in the middle of the text looks like a link to a quoted source, so they click or tap it and nothing happens. They also learn that blue does not reliably mean a link on this site, which weakens the real links.

findings.where: Hero, the 'Get in touch' button (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com); the address appears nowhere as text on the page
findings.fault: The page's one action only opens a mailto link, and the button's arrow suggests it goes to a page. The email address is never shown, so a visitor whose computer has no mail app set up gets nothing, or an unexpected desktop mail client, and has no address to copy.
findings.who_objects: Staff at a development bank, often on a locked-down work PC or using webmail. They click 'Get in touch', no page opens or the wrong mail app starts, and they cannot see Mark's address to write to him another way. The page's whole job fails for them.

findings.where: Motion sketch, 'Play again' (a button), next to the article specimen's 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' link
findings.fault: 'Play again' is a button that acts on this page, but it has exactly the look of a link: blue, underlined text, the same as the PDF link. One look means both 'go somewhere' and 'do something here'.
findings.who_objects: Whoever builds the next rounds from this tile. They would take the underlined-text look as the site's style for buttons, and a visitor would then mistake an on-page action for a link to another page.
